title_zh: 第二十一類 僧道騙

stories.title_en: A Monk Takes a Cow for His Mother

paragraphs.zh: 夏六月间，一行脚僧过于路，见小竖牧一伙牛。内有黄牝牛，大而肥。牧竖伸左脚与之舐，牝牛舐之；又与右脚与舐。僧问曰：“此牛何为舐你脚？”牧竖曰：“此牛最驯熟，吾甚爱之。我脚多汗咸，故牛爱舐。”僧知牛爱舐咸味，密此牛，系索长者家所畜的。
paragraphs.en: In the sixth month of summer a traveling monk was on the road and saw a herd-boy watching a group of cattle. Among them was a yellow cow, large and fat. The boy held out his left foot for it to lick, and the cow licked it; then he held out his right foot the same way. The monk asked, “Why does this cow lick your feet?” The boy said, “This cow is very tame. I am very fond of it. My feet sweat and taste of salt, so the cow likes to lick them.” The monk understood that cattle like a salty taste, and he quietly noted that this cow was one kept by Elder Suo.

paragraphs.zh: 次日，僧取浓盐汁，厚涂头脸及遍身手足等处，寻到索长者家，跪门涕泣曰：“愿赐慈悲心，超度我母子。”索老曰：“我不会说法念经，怎能超度人？”僧曰：“我先母在生，不肯修斋布福。今已死七年，知冥中必受罪谴，奈家贫不能功果追荐。因慕目连救母，情愿削发从师，专求度母。前月得遇善知识，指老母在长者家投生为黄牛母，敬来求超度。”索老曰：“我栏有四头牝牛，知何牛是？”僧曰：“愿同往看。畜物更有灵性，母子相见，必有恩爱情在，自与别的不同。”索老与僧同到栏前，放出群牛。僧见大牝牛到，即揭下袖蒂帽，涕泣跪向前曰：“此是吾母也！”牝牛嗅其咸味，以舌遍舐其头脸，若怜惜状。僧愈加流涕，又自剥去衣服，牛遍舐其身，不忍去。索老看见果异，真似母之爱子，但不能言耳。问曰：“既是你前生之母，今须何以超度？”僧曰：“我若有银，当以半价买去养，奈贫僧衣钵罄空。愿长者权舍贫僧，牵往山庵，日采草煮粥喂养。待其谴罪完满，天年数终，贫僧当收埋，念经卷超度，庶来世转身为人，不堕畜生道矣。”长者怜其词情恳切，曰：“吾舍与你去。”僧叩头拜谢，牵此牛往三日路外，付出庵寄养。
paragraphs.en: The next day the monk took thick salt brine and coated his head, face, whole body, hands, and feet with it, then found Elder Suo’s house. He knelt at the gate weeping and said, “Please show a compassionate heart and deliver my mother and me.” Elder Suo said, “I cannot preach or recite sutras. How could I deliver anyone?” The monk said, “While my late mother was alive she would not keep vegetarian fasts or give alms. She has been dead seven years, and I know she must be suffering punishment in the underworld, but our family is poor and I cannot afford the rites to save her. Admiring how Mulian saved his mother, I shaved my head and followed a teacher, seeking only to deliver her. Last month I met a good teacher who pointed out that my old mother had been reborn as a yellow cow in the elder’s house, so I have come respectfully to ask that she be delivered.” Elder Suo said, “I have four cows in the pen. How would one know which cow it is?” The monk said, “Please let me go and look with you. Beasts have even more spiritual nature. When mother and child meet, there will surely be affection, different from the others.” Elder Suo went with the monk to the pen and let the cattle out. When the monk saw the large cow arrive, he took off his cap, knelt forward weeping, and said, “This is my mother!” The cow smelled the salt and licked his head and face all over, as if pitying him. The monk wept still more, then stripped off his clothes himself; the cow licked his whole body and would not leave. Elder Suo saw that it truly was strange, just like a mother’s love for her child, only it could not speak. He asked, “If this is your mother from a former life, what must be done now to deliver her?” The monk said, “If I had silver, I would buy her at half price and raise her, but this poor monk’s robe and bowl are empty. I ask the elder to grant her to me for now. I will lead her to a mountain hermitage, pick grass each day, and cook gruel to feed her. When her punishment is complete and her natural span ends, I will bury her and recite sutras to deliver her, so that in the next life she may turn and become human and not fall into the animal path.” The elder pitied the earnestness of his words and said, “I grant her to you. Take her.” The monk kowtowed in thanks, led the cow three days’ journey away, and left her at a hermitage to be kept.

paragraphs.zh: 至十月，天气寒凉，叫屠子来宰，以一半分与，卖得价银一两五钱；一半僧自留，做成干粮，收藏衲袄中各处。径到索长者厅前，结双趺而坐。长者出曰：“何僧敢升厅而坐？”僧曰：“你颇认得我么？”长者曰：“不知你是何人，怎么认得？”僧曰：“亦自然觉得面熟么？”长者曰：“并无相会，何处面熟？”僧长叹曰：“你本来灵性且尽丧，何故不识故人色相！”长者曰：“何为是故人？”僧曰：“昔佛印点醒东坡，远公唤回乐天，非苏、白二公之故人乎？你前生与我同修，因尘心未断，复来享此人福。我今特来度你，急宜丢手尘债，再去勤修，庶不废前生功行也。”长者曰：“你安能识得前生？”僧曰：“我功行高你一倍。你今且享半生福禄，我又加半生苦修，何难知三生事因？”长者曰：“你今生若何苦修？”僧曰：“从前苦修且休提，现今已辟谷三年矣。”长者始惊曰：“你能辟谷，在我家辟一月何如？”僧笑曰：“三年于是，何有一月？”长者曰：“亦服茶汤乎？”僧曰：“清茶滚水，日一瓯耳。”长者留之，扫一空室与坐，早进瓯茶，夜进瓯滚水。
paragraphs.en: When the tenth month came and the weather turned cold, he called a butcher to slaughter her. He gave the butcher half, sold for one tael and five qian of silver; he kept the other half himself, made it into dried provisions, and hid them in various places in his patched robe. He went straight to Elder Suo’s hall and sat down in full lotus. The elder came out and said, “What monk dares come up into the hall and sit?” The monk said, “Do you rather recognize me?” The elder said, “I do not know who you are. How would I recognize you?” The monk said, “Do I not naturally look familiar?” The elder said, “We have never met. Where would the familiarity come from?” The monk sighed at length: “Your original spiritual nature is already lost completely. Why do you not know an old friend’s form?” The elder said, “What old friend?” The monk said, “In the past Foyin woke Dongpo, and Master Yuan called Letian back. Were they not old friends of Su and Bai? In a former life you cultivated together with me. Because your worldly heart was not cut off, you came back to enjoy these human blessings. I have come specially to deliver you. You should quickly drop worldly debts and go cultivate hard again, so as not to waste the merit of your former life.” The elder said, “How can you know former lives?” The monk said, “My merit is twice as high as yours. You are now enjoying half a lifetime of fortune, and I have added half a lifetime of bitter cultivation. Why would it be hard to know the causes of the three lives?” The elder said, “How have you bitterly cultivated in this life?” The monk said, “Never mind former bitter cultivation. I have already grain-fasted for three years.” The elder was startled at last: “If you can grain-fast, how about grain-fasting one month in my house?” The monk laughed: “Three years already—what is one month?” The elder said, “Do you still take tea and hot water?” The monk said, “Clear tea or boiling water, one bowl a day, that is all.” The elder kept him, swept an empty room for him to sit in, and sent in a bowl of tea in the morning and a bowl of boiling water at night.

paragraphs.zh: 连坐七日，再请出，答对如常。长者惊服，问曰：“我当如何修？”僧曰：“只弃家长往，自有修行善方。”长者曰：“妻寡子幼，产业付谁？此事不能。其次修何如？”僧曰：“唯有舍施，修寺奉佛，来生亦受福报。现今庐山一庵，化人独力修造。倘捐五百金，一完修之，亦一大功德也。”长者依言，遣仆同僧送五百金往，交付与住持明白，留仆住数日，送归报主。后僧分住持银二百五十两而去。其以辟谷动富翁，则私食所带之干粮耳，宁有人而真辟谷者！
paragraphs.en: He sat on like that for seven days, then was invited out again, and answered as usual. The elder was amazed and convinced, and asked, “How should I cultivate?” The monk said, “Just abandon the family and go far away; there are good methods of practice of themselves.” The elder said, “My wife would be left a widow and my children are young. Who would the property be given to? This I cannot do. What would the next-best cultivation be?” The monk said, “Only giving. Repair temples and serve the Buddha, and in the next life you will also receive blessed reward. Right now there is a hermitage on Mount Lu being rebuilt by one person’s donations. If you give five hundred taels and finish the repair in one stroke, that too is a great merit.” The elder followed his words, sent a servant with the monk to deliver five hundred taels, handed them clearly to the abbot, had the servant stay several days, then sent him home to report to his master. Later the monk split two hundred fifty taels of the abbot’s silver and left. As for moving the rich man by grain-fasting, he was privately eating the dried provisions he had brought. As if there were anyone who truly grain-fasts!

paragraphs.zh: 按：此僧脱牛，犹其小者，转卖之可也。名为生前母而宰食之，罪浮于天矣。至用为干粮而诈称辟谷，其骗亦大。虽半舍入庵，亦是好事，僧若得劝缘功。然周急赈贫，自当施于邻里，何必投入于庵？此愚人信福田利益之过也，亦未读傅奕公《高识传》矣。
paragraphs.en: Note: This monk’s stripping people of a cow was still the small part; he could have resold her. To name her his mother from her lifetime and then slaughter and eat her—the crime floats above Heaven. Then using her as dried provisions and falsely claiming to grain-fast: that swindle too was large. Though half the gift went into the hermitage, that was also a good deed, and the monk if he obtained the merit of urging the donation. But relieving the urgent and aiding the poor should of itself be given to neighbors. Why must it be thrown into a hermitage? This is the fault of fools who believe in the profits of the field of merit, and of not having read Master Fu Yi’s Gaoshi zhuan.

stories.title_en: Taking Infant Elixir to Fake Grain-Fasting

paragraphs.zh: 有僧自称能辟谷者，富家多召而试之。连七八日不食一粒，或间二三日，服滚汤一瓯而已。传名甚广，人争以金帛舍之。一乡官见褚县尊，偶道及此，称世间有此高僧，真仙佛再生于世出。褚公最正大，素不信僧道辈，曰：“人受此色身，哪能断绝食色？假托辟谷者，不过暗藏干粮，以哄惑愚民耳。明理君子，何可信此辈？若果能辟谷，彼将远遁深山，唯恐名落人间，何必浪游市里？受人施舍金帛，将何所用？”乡官被褚公一驳，似乎己为信邪，更欲取信其言，乃曰：“老父母不信，可召而试之，方知晚生言非妄矣。”
paragraphs.en: There was a monk who claimed he could grain-fast. Rich families often summoned him to test it. For seven or eight days running he would not eat a single grain, or every two or three days he would take only one bowl of boiling water. His name spread widely, and people competed to give him gold and silk. A local official, seeing Magistrate Chu, happened to mention this, saying the world had such an eminent monk, truly an immortal or Buddha born again. Master Chu was most upright, and had never believed monks and Daoists. He said, “People receive this physical body. How can they cut off food and sex? Those who pretend to grain-fast only hide dried provisions in secret, to fool the ignorant. How can a gentleman who understands principle believe this sort? If they could truly grain-fast, they would flee far into the deep mountains, fearing only that their names might fall among men. Why would they wander the markets? And if they accept gifts of gold and silk, what would they use them for?” The local official, rebuked by Master Chu, seemed as if he himself believed heresy, and wanted still more to make his words believed. So he said, “If Your Honor does not believe, you may summon him and test him, and then you will know this junior’s words are not false.”

paragraphs.zh: 褚公即差人唤至，令搜其身。别无夹带，唯持二十四个弥陀珠，诛之带入。扫一净室，布床席与坐，外遣人轮番密窥。日遣人明开门一视，出仍锁门。两日内，果结双趺而坐，容貌如故。第三日开视，见脸有乏汗，求滚水饮。褚公命与之，复出锁门。密窥者来禀曰：“僧以一弥陀珠调水饮讫，容貌复好。”后每两日进滚汤一碗，密窥者辄禀云：“以珠调吃。”
paragraphs.en: Master Chu at once sent men to call him in, and ordered his person searched. He had nothing else hidden on him, only twenty-four Amitabha beads, which they allowed him to bring in. They swept a clean room, spread a bed and mat for him to sit on, and outside sent people in rotation to watch in secret. Each day they sent someone to open the door openly and look once, then lock it again on leaving. For two days he did sit in full lotus, his looks unchanged. On the third day they opened and looked: his face had tired sweat, and he asked for boiling water to drink. Master Chu ordered it given, then they went out and locked the door again. The secret watchers came and reported: “The monk mixed one Amitabha bead in the water and drank it, and his looks recovered.” After that, every two days they sent in one bowl of boiling water, and the secret watchers always reported, “He mixed a bead and ate it.”

paragraphs.zh: 经十一日，召之出，取其弥陀珠视之，止十九枚在手耳。褚公收其珠，命收入轻监不许揽动，听彼静坐，以候发落。密嘱禁子曰。“铁容僧道人入见，两日后必问你乞食。你问其弥陀珠何以做？做来以水调之，与此珠一样，后重赏你。”
paragraphs.en: After eleven days they summoned him out, took his Amitabha beads and looked: only nineteen were still in his hands. Master Chu confiscated the beads, ordered him put in light detention and not to be disturbed, and let him sit quietly pending disposal. He secretly instructed the jailer: “Do not allow monks or Daoists to come in and see him. After two days he will surely beg you for food. Ask him how the Amitabha beads are made. If he makes some that, mixed with water, are the same as these beads, I will reward you heavily afterward.”

paragraphs.zh: 次日，僧即问禁子求食。禁子曰：“你教我作珠方法，便与你食。”僧曰：“此药极难得。你但与我食，出外多以银谢你，不必问此方。”禁子不与之食，三日饿倒，面青黄无人色矣。
paragraphs.en: The next day the monk asked the jailer for food. The jailer said, “Teach me the method for making the beads, and I will give you food.” The monk said, “This medicine is extremely hard to get. Just give me food. When I get out I will thank you with much silver. No need to ask for this formula.” The jailer gave him no food. After three days he collapsed from hunger, his face green-yellow, with no human color left.

paragraphs.zh: 褚公提出，审曰：“我早知此珠是孩儿丹矣。你供出制造方法来，免汝一死。”僧诈作将死形状，不敢应。褚公笑曰：“众看此辟谷僧，在褚爷前辟三日谷，即饿死矣。此丹妇人胎内孩子，必须谋死孕妇，剖其婴孩，以作此丹。不知你害死多少命，以造此恶业，你怎敢说出口？我岂求汝方乎？若打死你，罪还轻。”命衙前搭起一台，以十九枚珠发出，将四个调与众百姓看，以滚水调之，满碗都是膏液。有敢饮者，又香又甜，只饮两口，一日亦饱。后十五枚发与医生治补损。然后缚此僧在台上凌迟之。褚公曰：“县令为民父母，岂忍杀人？但为众冤泄恨矣。”众皆称快，而乡官后亦永不信僧道矣。
paragraphs.en: Master Chu had him brought out and examined him, saying, “I knew early on that these beads were infant elixir. Confess the method of manufacture, and I will spare you one death.” The monk pretended to be about to die, and dared not answer. Master Chu laughed: “Everyone look at this grain-fasting monk. Before Magistrate Chu he grain-fasted three days and is about to starve to death. This elixir is a child from a woman’s womb. You must plot to kill a pregnant woman and cut out the infant in order to make this elixir. Who knows how many lives you have destroyed to make this evil work—how dare you speak the formula aloud? As if I wanted your recipe? If I beat you to death, the punishment would still be light.” He ordered a platform built in front of the yamen, issued the nineteen beads, and had four mixed for the common people to see: mixed with boiling water, the whole bowl became a paste. Those who dared drink found it both fragrant and sweet; two mouthfuls and they were full for a day. The remaining fifteen were given to doctors to treat injuries and deficiencies. Then they bound this monk on the platform and put him to death by slicing. Master Chu said, “A county magistrate is father and mother to the people. How could he bear to kill? But this is to vent the hatred of the many wronged.” All called it satisfying, and afterward the local official never again believed monks and Daoists.

paragraphs.zh: 按：此诈辟谷者，多是藏干粮，其服孩儿丹者少。此粮非藏于身，恐人搜也。都寄于丐乞者之身，有人试之，则密以干粮付。又有服松毛竹叶者，松毛用羊蹄草同吃，竹叶用嫩蕨同吃，皆滑而可食。僧亦尝以此惑人，谓彼能服此。然从古有辟谷之说者，乃仙方，非人间所有也。曾见有遇异人授辟谷者，述之于左。
paragraphs.en: Note: Those who fake grain-fasting mostly hide dried provisions; those who take infant elixir are few. This food is not hidden on the body, for fear people will search. It is all entrusted to beggars’ bodies; when someone tests them, they secretly pass the dried provisions over. There are also those who take pine needles and bamboo leaves: pine needles eaten together with yangti herb, bamboo leaves eaten together with tender ferns, all slippery and edible. Monks have also used this to fool people, saying they can live on these. But from ancient times, the grain-fasting methods that exist are immortal recipes, not things of the human world. I once heard of someone who met an extraordinary person who taught grain-fasting; I record it below.

paragraphs.zh: 武夷山有贫民结庐于岩曲，仅容床灶，垦山种茶，卖以供食。积十数年，所开茶山，岁可收鬻三四金，每日力作不息，唯大寒、暑甚、风雨，终日寂坐岩庐下，不识经典，亦不通往来。
paragraphs.en: On Mount Wuyi a poor man built a hut in a bend of the cliffs, barely room for a bed and a stove. He opened the mountain and planted tea, selling it to feed himself. After ten-odd years the tea slopes he had opened could be harvested and sold for three or four taels a year. Every day he labored without rest; only in severe cold, extreme heat, or wind and rain would he sit silent all day under the cliff hut. He did not know the scriptures, and also had no dealings with others.

paragraphs.zh: 忽一日一道人过其庐，谓曰：“汝耕山劳苦，何不以茶山付人代耕，岁收一金，以买衣资？吾授汝辟谷方，则不须买米，不劳耕山，可安坐自足矣。”山民曰：“吾尝间修行人有辟谷方，若肯教我，愿拜师父求学。”道士曰：“你性子恬静，尽可修行。今后唯早晨煎清泉二罐，煎至半落，以两罐合煎作一罐，早午晚各饮二瓯。饮后澄心息想，以舌抵上颚，合口闭目，终日静坐。或天清神爽，爰出游，行则慢步闲观，随意所适，不拘半午，不拘片时。凡行住坐卧，只从心不拂。或山果草实可食者，遇着稍食一二不妨，但不可有意寻求。如此便可辟谷矣。记之不可轻易传人。”山民依此行之，一年果不食一黍，颜如金黄，轻健如常。同山旁居人，常不见其籴米，或过其庐，亦无锅甑。问之，答曰：“近年学得辟谷方。”居人转相传异。有拜之求方者，辄逃避不授，曰：“师嘱勿轻传泄。”次年传于远近，多有来册拜访者。或赍粮宿其居庐看守，至匝月，果唯见饮滚水，饮后静坐，寂无一为，亦无闲谈。不知者或穷问之，或与谈修养，微笑而起，出游山径，迨午晚归，复暖滚水而饮。凡人之来者不迎，去者不送，亦无半语讯问人。人问之，有可答者，随口答一二句。问其餘闲事，则摇首不应，若有厌烦之意，唯自去静坐。凡言动应酬，总是付之无心而已。第二年后，名益著。富家贵人，多备鞍轿迎者，坚逃不往。富贵人身往劝逼之，后亦遍往诸家，所到不食人一物，唯向空室静坐，若一木佛，然有言动而已。
paragraphs.en: Suddenly one day a Daoist passed his hut and said, “You till the mountain and labor hard. Why not give the tea slopes to someone else to till, take one tael a year to buy clothes, and let me teach you a grain-fasting method? Then you need not buy rice or labor at tilling, and can sit at ease and be sufficient.” The mountain man said, “I have heard in passing that practitioners have grain-fasting methods. If you are willing to teach me, I will bow to you as master and ask to learn.” The Daoist said, “Your nature is quiet; you are quite able to cultivate. From now on, in the morning only boil two jars of clear spring water down by half, then combine the two jars and boil them into one. Morning, noon, and evening drink two bowls each time. After drinking, still the mind and rest thought, press the tongue to the upper palate, close the mouth and shut the eyes, and sit quietly all day. Or if the sky is clear and the spirit fresh, then go out walking: walk slowly and look at leisure, following whatever suits you, whether half a day or only a moment. In walking, standing, sitting, and lying, only follow the mind and do not go against it. Or if there are mountain fruits and plant seeds that can be eaten, if you come upon them it does no harm to eat one or two, but you must not seek them on purpose. In this way you can grain-fast. Remember this, and do not lightly pass it to others.” The mountain man followed this and practiced it. After one year he indeed did not eat a single grain of millet; his face was gold-yellow, and he was light and strong as usual. People living on the same mountain nearby often did not see him buy rice; or if they passed his hut, there was also no pot or steamer. When they asked, he answered, “In recent years I have learned a grain-fasting method.” The neighbors passed the wonder from one to another. Those who bowed and asked for the method he would always flee and not teach, saying, “My teacher ordered me not to leak it lightly.” The next year it spread near and far, and many came with visiting cards to pay respects. Some brought grain and lodged in his hut to watch, for a full month: they indeed saw him only drink boiling water, then sit quietly after drinking, silent, doing nothing at all, and with no idle talk. Those who did not understand might question him hard, or talk with him of cultivation; he would smile, rise, and go walk the mountain paths, returning at noon or evening, then warm boiling water and drink again. Of people who came he did not welcome them; of those who left he did not see them off; he also did not ask people half a word. If people asked him, and there was something he could answer, he would answer one or two sentences offhand. If they asked about other idle matters, he would shake his head and not answer, as if annoyed, and only go sit quietly himself. All speech, movement, and social response he simply put down as no-mind. After the second year his name was still more famous. Rich houses and noble men often prepared saddles and sedan chairs to receive him; he firmly fled and would not go. When the rich and noble went in person to urge and press him, he later also went around to the various houses. Wherever he arrived he would not eat a single thing of theirs, only sit quietly in an empty room, like a wooden Buddha, with only some speech and movement.

paragraphs.zh: 经二年半后，有潭阳富人礼迎之，虔奉更肃，若敬神明。时进茶果，稍为食些少。后备清茶精饭，苦劝之食，坚辞不能，不得已为食一瓯。少顷饥甚，服滚汤。又饥饿不能禁，又索食。富人欢喜，肃进之。连三日内，皆一日五食，仅能止饥。山民自惊疑，急求归山，依旧服汤静坐，不免肚饥。后只得复食，三餐如寻常人矣。
paragraphs.en: After two and a half years a rich man of Tanyang received him with ceremony, serving him still more solemnly, as if honoring a god. From time to time he sent in tea and fruit, and the man ate a little. Later he prepared clear tea and fine rice and bitterly urged him to eat. He firmly declined that he could not; then, unable to help it, he ate one bowl. In a short while he was very hungry, and took boiling water. He was hungry again and could not bear it, and asked for food once more. The rich man was glad and served him solemnly. For three days running he ate five times a day, and only then could stop the hunger. The mountain man was startled and doubtful himself, and urgently asked to return to the mountain. He took water and sat quietly as before, but could not avoid a hungry belly. Later he had no choice but to eat again, three meals like an ordinary person.

paragraphs.zh: 按：山民所遇之道士，明是仙人。若辟谷三年完满，必有超度矣。惜哉为名所累，致人迎奉，致人逼食，而自毁前功。此劝食之愚。富人彼意，欲虔奉之，以分生佛之福，岂诚心奉道哉！此山民既为所误，而彼福亦安在也？且堕百劫之罪，来生必与山民结一大仇矣。观此，则辟谷乃仙方，不徒在服滚水静坐也。不然，后仍服之坐之，而何谷不能辟哉？则今之托辟谷索人钱米者，真盗贼僧道也。真辟谷者，敢令人知乎？
paragraphs.en: Note: The Daoist the mountain man met was clearly an immortal. If the three years of grain-fasting had been completed, there would surely have been deliverance. A pity he was burdened by fame, which brought people to receive and serve him, brought people to force him to eat, and he destroyed his former achievement himself. This was the folly of urging him to eat. That rich man’s intent was to serve him devoutly in order to share a living Buddha’s blessings. Was that a sincere heart serving the Way? This mountain man had already been harmed by it, and where then was that man’s blessing? He will also fall into the sin of a hundred kalpas, and in the next life he must form a great enmity with the mountain man. Looking at this, grain-fasting is an immortal method, not merely a matter of drinking boiling water and sitting still. Otherwise, afterward he still drank it and sat it—why then could grain not be fasted? So those today who plead grain-fasting in order to demand people’s money and rice are truly thief-monks and Daoists. Would a true grain-faster dare let people know?

stories.title_en: Believing a Monk’s Talk, He Nearly Came to Ruin

paragraphs.zh: 徽州人丁达，为人好善喜舍。一日，与友林泽往海澄买椒木，到临清等处发卖，货已卖讫。此处有一寺，内有名僧号无二者，年近三十餘，相貌俊雅，会讲经典，善谈因果，风动多少良家子弟，往寺参拜，常有被其劝化，削发出家者。时丁达邀林泽去谒无二。林泽曰：“你素性好善，闻此僧巧嘴善言，累诱人削发为僧。你若见之，被其哄惑，何以归见父母？”达曰：“劝在彼，从在我。我自有主，彼何能拿？”若要往拜之。见无二举动闲雅，谈及因果之事，达被打动，尽舍其财本，入寺拜无二为师，欲削发为僧。泽怒曰：“未到此处，我早言之。今果被哄惑，何以为人？”再三苦谏不听。泽自回去，达在寺修行。
paragraphs.en: Ding Da of Huizhou was a man who liked goodness and liked to give. One day he went with his friend Lin Ze to Haicheng to buy pepper-wood, and sold it at Linqing and other places; the goods were already sold off. In that place there was a temple, and in it a famous monk styled Wuer, nearly thirty-odd, of handsome looks, able to lecture on the scriptures and good at talking of karmic cause and effect. He moved any number of sons of good families to go to the temple and pay respects; often they were converted by him and shaved their heads to leave home. At the time Ding Da invited Lin Ze to go visit Wuer. Lin Ze said, “You have always liked goodness. I hear this monk has a clever mouth and good talk, and has repeatedly lured people to shave and become monks. If you see him and are fooled by him, how will you go home and face your parents?” Da said, “Persuasion is on his side; following is on mine. I have my own master within. How can he take me?” And he insisted on going to pay respects. He saw that Wuer’s manner was easy and refined, and when they talked of karmic matters Da was moved. He gave away all his trading capital, entered the temple, bowed to Wuer as his teacher, and wanted to shave his head and become a monk. Ze was angry: “Before we even reached this place I already said it. Now you have indeed been fooled. How can you still be a man?” He bitterly advised him again and again; Da would not listen. Ze went back by himself, and Da stayed in the temple to cultivate.

paragraphs.zh: 过二年后，僧无二因有董寡妇入寺烧香，容貌甚美，亦信善好念弥陀。带一使女，十七岁，国色娇媚，到寺亦参拜。无二以巧言劝诱，寡妇亦心服，即拜无二为师，欲削发为尼，暂在寺宿几夜。其丫头常往无二房送果吕，无二欲心难制，以白金十两戏之。丫头收其银，与之通情。无二又思及其嫠妇，夜潜入其房，候董氏熟睡，欲强奸之。董氏坚贞不从，喊曰：“何人无理，敢来奸盗？”言未数声，无二以手巾紧勒其颈，须臾而死。
paragraphs.en: After two years the monk Wuer, because Widow Dong came to the temple to burn incense—she was very beautiful, and also believed in goodness and liked to recite Amitabha. She brought a maid, seventeen, of national beauty and charm, who also paid respects at the temple. Wuer used clever words to persuade and lure; the widow’s heart also submitted. She at once bowed to Wuer as her teacher, wanted to shave her head and become a nun, and stayed a few nights in the temple for the time being. Her maid often went to Wuer’s room to deliver fruit. Wuer could not restrain desire, and used ten taels of white silver to sport with her. The maid took the silver and had relations with him. Wuer then thought also of the widow. At night he slipped into her room, waited until Dong-shi was in a deep sleep, and tried to rape her. Dong-shi was chaste and firm and would not comply. She cried out, “What person is so lawless, daring to come to rape and steal?” Before she had spoken many sounds, Wuer tightened a handkerchief around her neck, and in a moment she was dead.

paragraphs.zh: 次日，使女去报知董氏之子李英。及到寺，无二已先逃走矣。但无二久出名，各处人多认得。李英雇人遍处缉拿，不两日拿到送县。王爷即点民兵百餘，围绕其寺。时寺僧已四散逃命，无僧可拿。王爷再命焚其寺，将无二责了四十，问典刑之罪。
paragraphs.en: The next day the maid went and reported to Dong-shi’s son Li Ying. By the time they reached the temple, Wuer had already fled first. But Wuer had long been famous, and people in all places mostly recognized him. Li Ying hired men to hunt him everywhere; in less than two days they caught him and sent him to the county. Magistrate Wang at once mustered a hundred-odd militia and surrounded the temple. By then the temple monks had already scattered in all directions to save their lives; there was no monk who could be seized. Magistrate Wang further ordered the temple burned, had Wuer beaten forty strokes, and sentenced him to the capital penalty.

paragraphs.zh: 达悔财本俱丧，无颜回家。后家中已知达逃回，叫人寻觅归家，发长方敢出。此愚人信僧之明鉴也。
paragraphs.en: Da regretted that his capital was all lost, and had no face to go home. Later his family already knew Da had fled back, sent people to find him and bring him home, and only when his hair had grown long did he dare go out. This is a clear mirror of fools who believe monks.

paragraphs.zh: 按：寺门藏奸，僧徒即贼，此是常事，亦往往有败露者。人不目见，亦多耳闻，何犹不知戒？而妇人入寺，男子出家，真大愚也。董虽死犹幸完节；丁达虽幸逃生而财本已丧。使当时与无二并获，何分清浊？必并死狱中矣。故邪说引诱人者，无论士农工商，皆当勿信而远之可也。
paragraphs.en: Note: Temple gates hide villains, and monks are thieves. This is a common matter, and there are also often cases that come to light. If people have not seen it with their eyes, they have also often heard it with their ears. Why do they still not know to take warning? And women entering temples, men leaving home—truly great folly. Dong, though she died, was still fortunate to keep her chastity complete; Ding Da, though fortunate to escape with his life, had already lost his capital. If at the time he had been taken together with Wuer, how would they have told clean from dirty? He would surely have died in prison with him. So those who use heretical talk to lure people, whether scholar, farmer, artisan, or merchant, should all not believe it, and keep far from it.

stories.title_en: A Monk Who Looked Like the Guardian God Fakes a Subscription

paragraphs.zh: 天元寺年久倾颓，住持僧完朗有意修之，恐工费浩大，非有大力者发愿独任，未易举手。忽一日，游方僧若冰来寺投宿，身干魁梧，面方而黑，目圆耳长，宛似本寺伽蓝形象。完朗一见心喜，夜设斋款待，甚加勤敬。次日，僧若冰曰：“宝刹非兴旺，何如此肯接待十方？”完朗曰：“兴我寺者，在尊宿一臂之力，敢大有所托。”若冰曰：“山家缘薄，怎能相助？”完朗曰：“此寺须五百金方可全修，虽化些少众缘，亦不济事。看尊相，极似我本寺伽蓝，托你择巨富家，若化其全修，待彼在允否间，约其来寺亲看，我自有方法纳之。”
paragraphs.en: Tianyuan Temple had been dilapidated for years. The abbot Wanlang meant to repair it, but feared the labor and cost would be huge: unless some person of great power vowed to take it on alone, it would not be easy to raise a hand. Suddenly one day the wandering monk Ruobing came to the temple to lodge. He was tall and sturdy, with a square black face, round eyes and long ears, exactly like the image of this temple’s Qielan guardian. Wanlang was delighted at the sight, set a vegetarian feast that night to receive him, and treated him with extra diligence and respect. The next day the monk Ruobing said, “This precious monastery is not flourishing. Why then are you willing to receive the ten directions like this?” Wanlang said, “The one who will raise my temple is in your reverence’s one arm of strength. I dare greatly to rely on you.” Ruobing said, “This mountain household’s karmic ties are thin. How can I help?” Wanlang said, “This temple needs five hundred taels before it can be fully repaired. Even collecting a little from many donors will not serve. Looking at your honored appearance, you extremely resemble our temple’s Qielan. I ask you to pick a hugely rich family. If you collect from them for the full repair, wait until they are between agreeing and not, arrange for them to come to the temple and look in person, and I will have a method of my own to take them in.”

paragraphs.zh: 若冰会意，前去大江边，有柴商财本巨万。若冰备干粮在身，直到柴排厅中，朗讽一经，结趺而坐，高叫曰：“化缘！”柴商荆秀云命手下以钱与之。僧全不视，曰：“吾非化小可钱钞。贫僧与施主有夙缘，要化千金。”秀云作色曰：“化千金何用？”僧曰：“此去二百里，有天元寺。前创时，施主有缘在，故今生大富。近年颓坏，须五百金修理，又须五百金为香灯田，后可保长久，则施主功德远大矣。”秀云曰：“你为寺化疏，前生与此寺何缘？”僧曰：“寺本我居食之地，非有缘，得久居乎？”秀云不睬之。僧在柴排坐三日不去，手下人以饭与食，亦食；不与，亦不食。又过四日，秀云曰：“吾舍三百相助，你更去化别人。”僧曰：“有缘者不能化，无缘者何劳空说？”秀云曰：“你把疏簿来，我题三百两。”僧曰：“疏簿在寺中。三百亦不够用，不须题？你图今生享福，只施五百两。若布来世津梁，非千金不可。”秀云曰：“吾不信今生来生，你且领三百两去，好心修造。不足者，岂无别善人相助？”僧曰：“吾哪要银？你自送与住持僧。”秀云曰：“吾十日后送到寺来。”僧遂合掌，念“阿弥陀佛”一声而去。归对完朗详说其事，又约“十日后柴商且来，吾远避之。”完朗大喜，早备茶果斋品以待。
paragraphs.en: Ruobing understood. He went forward to the edge of the great river, where there was a firewood merchant with capital in the tens of thousands. Ruobing packed dried provisions on his person, went straight into the timber-raft hall, loudly chanted a sutra, sat in lotus, and called out, “Collecting alms!” The firewood merchant Jing Xiuyun ordered his men to give him cash. The monk did not look at it at all, and said, “I am not collecting paltry cash. This poor monk has a former-life tie with the donor, and wants to collect a thousand taels.” Xiuyun changed color: “What use is collecting a thousand taels?” The monk said, “Two hundred li from here is Tianyuan Temple. When it was first founded, the donor had a tie there, and so in this life you are greatly rich. In recent years it has fallen into ruin. It needs five hundred taels for repairs, and another five hundred taels for incense-and-lamp fields; afterward it can be kept long, and then the donor’s merit will be far and great.” Xiuyun said, “You are collecting a subscription for the temple. What tie did you have with this temple in a former life?” The monk said, “The temple is originally the place where I live and eat. Without a tie, could I dwell there long?” Xiuyun paid him no attention. The monk sat on the timber raft three days and would not leave. The men gave him rice, and he ate; if they did not give it, he also did not eat. After four more days Xiuyun said, “I will give three hundred to help. You go collect from others besides.” The monk said, “If I cannot collect from the one with the tie, why waste empty talk on those without a tie?” Xiuyun said, “Bring the subscription book. I will write three hundred taels.” The monk said, “The subscription book is at the temple. Three hundred is also not enough to use. No need to write it. If you only seek to enjoy blessings in this life, just give five hundred taels. If you would lay a ford and bridge for the next life, nothing less than a thousand taels will do.” Xiuyun said, “I do not believe in this life and the next. You take three hundred taels and go, and kindly do the building. If it is not enough, will there be no other good people to help?” The monk said, “Why would I want the silver? You send it yourself to the abbot.” Xiuyun said, “I will send it to the temple in ten days.” The monk then put his palms together, recited “Amitabha Buddha” once, and left. He returned and told Wanlang the matter in detail, and also arranged, “In ten days the firewood merchant will come. I will stay far away.” Wanlang was greatly pleased, and early prepared tea, fruit, and vegetarian dishes to wait.

paragraphs.zh: 至第十日，秀云果带银同两仆来。完朗知是柴商，肃迎待茶毕，问曰：“施主高姓？”秀云曰：“姓荆。”完朗曰：“施主从哪里来？”秀云曰：“前约宝刹中化疏僧，今敬从江上来。”完朗沉吟曰：“山寺未曾化疏。”秀云曰：“十七日前，有僧在柴楼中坐七日，我许他今日来。”完朗曰：“本寺僧此半月内并无人出外者，必方僧诈托也。”即命作斋相待。秀云心疑怪：“若方僧诈托，何不前日即领银去？”只存在心，遍寺闲游。到伽蓝祠去，举头看伽蓝宛似前日僧形象。两仆亦指曰：“此伽蓝好似前日僧。”秀云看越惊异，心疑是伽蓝化为僧，以劝我修寺。即以祈曰：“前日僧若是你变的，求一圣。”即打一圣。又曰：“三百金已带来，祈保今年大利。”再一圣，又得一阳。又曰：“三百不够，若要五百，求一圣。”又得一阴。”又祝曰：“我心中已悟。若更要五百两香灯，求一圣。”果掷一圣。秀云拜谢讫，来就斋席，谓完朗曰：“须用银几何？”完朗曰：“久有意要修。前日叫匠人估计，要五百两方够，故不敢举。”秀云曰：“我前日许过三百两，今现送在此，明日更送二百两来添。若修完备，再舍五百两买置香灯田，永远奉佛。”完朗闻言大喜，合掌下拜。后依约舍完，若冰密分二百两而去。
paragraphs.en: On the tenth day Xiuyun indeed brought silver and came with two servants. Wanlang knew it was the firewood merchant, received him with ceremony, finished serving tea, and asked, “What is the donor’s honored surname?” Xiuyun said, “Jing.” Wanlang said, “Where has the donor come from?” Xiuyun said, “I previously arranged with the subscription monk of this precious monastery. Now I have respectfully come up from the river.” Wanlang pondered: “This mountain temple has not been collecting subscriptions.” Xiuyun said, “Seventeen days ago a monk sat in my timber loft for seven days. I promised him I would come today.” Wanlang said, “In this past half month none of this temple’s monks have gone out. It must be a wandering monk falsely claiming it.” He at once ordered a vegetarian meal prepared. Xiuyun thought it strange in his heart: if a wandering monk was falsely claiming it, why did he not take the silver that day? He only kept it in mind, and wandered the whole temple at leisure. He went to the Qielan shrine, raised his head, and looked: the Qielan was exactly like the monk of the other day. The two servants also pointed and said, “This Qielan looks very like the monk from before.” Xiuyun looked and was still more amazed, and suspected in his heart that the Qielan had transformed into a monk in order to urge him to repair the temple. He then prayed: “If the monk of the other day was you transformed, grant one holy cast.” He at once threw the blocks and got one holy sign. He said again, “I have already brought three hundred taels. Pray that this year there be great profit.” He threw once more, and got a yang. He said again, “Three hundred is not enough. If you want five hundred, grant one holy cast.” He again got a yin. He blessed again: “I have already understood in my heart. If you further want five hundred taels for incense-and-lamp, grant one holy cast.” Indeed he threw one holy sign. Xiuyun bowed his thanks, came to the vegetarian feast, and said to Wanlang, “How much silver must be used?” Wanlang said, “I have long meant to repair it. The other day I had craftsmen estimate: it will take five hundred taels to be enough, so I dared not start.” Xiuyun said, “The other day I promised three hundred taels. I now deliver them here, and tomorrow I will send two hundred more to add. When the repair is complete, I will further give five hundred taels to buy incense-and-lamp fields, to serve the Buddha forever.” Wanlang heard this and was greatly pleased, put his palms together and bowed. Later Xiuyun gave it all as agreed, and Ruobing secretly took two hundred taels as his split and left.

paragraphs.zh: 按：僧貌似伽蓝，故凑成此巧，亦可谓奇。然是人作成此套，何尝真有伽蓝化身乎！故富而能舍，本是善行；若谓真佛化缘而施舍者辄有福报，此两个装骗僧，岂能福人乎？吾不信也。
paragraphs.en: Note: The monk’s looks resembled the Qielan, so this trick was pieced together; one may also call it remarkable. But it was people who made up this setup. When was there ever a true Qielan incarnation? So being rich and able to give is originally a good deed. If one says that a true Buddha collecting alms, and those who give, always have blessed reward—could these two monks who staged a swindle bless anyone? I do not believe it.

stories.title_en: Falsely Claiming Foresight to Cheat a Silk Robe

paragraphs.zh: 东阳江达涧，父遗产万金。因为本府库吏累累浸润剥削，破去家产强半；又好男风，尝畜美好小仆，陪侍出入。有日，江之梁友遇其小仆，问曰：“前日为你相公买两匹青绢都长，做长衫必有剩。”小仆曰：“裁工不善做，先做一领太长，穿不得；后一领做得恰好。”梁曰：“长的可裁短，何妨？”仆曰：“他也不要得，已藏在书房大箱中去。”———原来江多衣服，其穿后不用的，都投入此箱。梁曰：“新服何忍弃，叫把与我修短服之。”仆曰：“你要问他讨，箱中第三件便是这新服。”
paragraphs.en: Jiang Dajian of Dongyang inherited ten thousand taels from his father. Because as a prefectural treasury clerk he was repeatedly soaked and pared away, more than half his family property was wrecked. He also liked male favorites, and often kept handsome young servants to attend him going out and in. One day Jiang’s friend Liang met his young servant and asked, “The other day two bolts of dark silk bought for your master were both long. Making a long robe there must be leftover.” The servant said, “The tailor was not good at the work. The first one he made was too long and cannot be worn; the later one was made just right.” Liang said, “The long one can be cut shorter. What harm?” The servant said, “He does not want it either. It has already been put away in the big chest in the study.”—Originally Jiang had many clothes; those he no longer used after wearing them were all thrown into this chest. Liang said, “How can one bear to throw away a new robe? Tell him to give it to me to alter shorter and wear.” The servant said, “If you want to ask him for it, the third piece in the chest is this new robe.”

paragraphs.zh: 适一僧在旁闻得，素知江达涧肯施舍，即诈称方僧，入江相公廨中抄化。江以两文钱施之。僧曰：“吾看满衙之中，皆有怨气，唯相公府中祥光满室，后日必有好官职，前程远大。吾将化你一件好服，以结个缘。”江曰：“我无好服。”僧曰：“你有一件穿不得的，舍与我好。”江故曰：“衣皆可穿，哪有穿不得的？”僧曰：“是一件新青绢太长的，在书房大箱中，第三件该舍与我，吾为尔消灾延寿。不然，你眼下有多少是非到。”江心异之，开大箱中看，果有两件在上，新绢服第三。便疑此僧先知，持出舍与之，问曰：“既舍此服，可免是非否？”僧曰：“我试你有善心否。今果肯施，便转灾成福矣。”
paragraphs.en: A monk standing nearby happened to hear this. He had long known that Jiang Dajian was willing to give, so he pretended to be a wandering monk and went into Master Jiang’s yamen quarters to collect alms. Jiang gave him two cash. The monk said, “I look through the whole yamen: there is resentful qi everywhere. Only in your honor’s residence auspicious light fills the rooms. Later you will surely have a good official post and a far future. I will collect one good robe from you, to form a tie.” Jiang said, “I have no good robes.” The monk said, “You have one that cannot be worn. Give it to me; that will be good.” Jiang therefore said, “The clothes can all be worn. How would there be one that cannot be worn?” The monk said, “It is one new dark-silk robe that is too long, in the big chest in the study. The third piece should be given to me. I will dispel disaster for you and extend your life. Otherwise you have much trouble arriving right before your eyes.” Jiang thought it strange in his heart, opened the big chest and looked: indeed there were two pieces on top, and the new silk robe was the third. He then suspected this monk had foresight, took it out and gave it to him, and asked, “Having given this robe, can I be spared the trouble?” The monk said, “I was testing whether you have a good heart. Now you are indeed willing to give, so disaster has already turned into fortune.”

paragraphs.zh: 按：今僧皆庸人，何能前知？其称已往事者，多得于传闻；说未来事者，皆涉于矫诬。观此僧欺江相公之事，则今之称善知识者，皆此类也。江相公之易欺如此，家安得不败？世之信僧引诱者，可以此为鉴。
paragraphs.en: Note: Monks today are all ordinary men. How can they know the future? When they speak of past events, they mostly get them from hearsay; when they speak of future events, they all involve false claims. Looking at this monk’s cheating of Master Jiang, then those today who call themselves good teachers are all of this type. Master Jiang was so easy to cheat—how could the household not fail? Those in the world who believe monks’ lures may take this as a warning.
